summary: Ozenoxacin (XEPI) is a nonfluorinated quinolone antimicrobial formulated as a 1% topical cream. It is FDA-approved for the topical treatment of impetigo due to Staphylococcus aureus (including MRSA isolates) or Streptococcus pyogenes in patients 2 months of age and older. It is bactericidal and applied as a thin layer twice daily for 5 days. Systemic absorption after topical application is negligible, so systemic safety considerations (renal, hepatic, pregnancy, lactation) are minimal. For topical use only.
indications: Topical treatment of impetigo due to Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes in adult and pediatric patients 2 months of age and older

moa: Ozenoxacin is a quinolone antimicrobial that inhibits the bacterial DNA replication enzymes DNA gyrase A and topoisomerase IV, blocking DNA replication. It is bactericidal against Staphylococcus aureus (including methicillin-resistant isolates) and Streptococcus pyogenes.

preg: No human pregnancy data. Systemic absorption following topical application is negligible, so fetal exposure is not expected. Oral ozenoxacin toxicity studies in pregnant rats and rabbits showed no significant adverse developmental effects at exposures far exceeding those seen with dermal application.
lact: No data on presence in human milk. Because systemic absorption after topical application is negligible, exposure of the breastfed infant is not expected. Weigh developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding against maternal need.
renal: No relevant systemic exposure following topical application; no dosage adjustment needed.
hepatic: No relevant systemic exposure following topical application; no dosage adjustment needed. Ozenoxacin is minimally metabolized in human hepatocytes.

minor: In vitro antagonism with ciprofloxacin against S. aureus (clinical relevance limited given topical use)

missed: Apply the missed dose as soon as remembered, then continue the regular twice-daily schedule. If it is nearly time for the next application, skip the missed dose - do not apply extra cream.
overdose: Any sign or symptom of overdose, whether topical or from accidental ingestion, should be treated symptomatically. There is no specific antidote.
